f2_binding.current_scope: deterministic caller-supplied transition evidence only; no provider/audio/VAD runtime

external_primary_observations.finding: conversation.item.truncate is specifically defined for interruption when model audio has been delivered faster than realtime but not fully played. The client supplies assistant item_id plus audio_end_ms so the server conversation is synchronized to client playback; the unplayed transcript portion is removed from server context.
response.cancel cancels an in-progress response and produces response.done with cancelled status; response_id can bind cancellation to the specific response.
For WebRTC/SIP, output_audio_buffer.clear cuts off current audio and should be preceded by response.cancel. The cleared event carries response_id.

hypothesis.statement: WP705's current BARGE_IN evidence is sufficient as an abstract user-input transition marker, but it is insufficient by itself to prove provider-bound heard-history correctness. A future realtime adapter can observe user barge-in while the server still retains assistant audio/text the user never heard unless the adapter separately binds interruption to the exact assistant output and heard cutoff/truncation evidence.

counterhypothesis.statement: No WP705 core change is required because realtime_reentry.py is intentionally provider-neutral and caller-supplied; a provider adapter can prove playback synchronization elsewhere and only emit BARGE_IN after that proof is complete.
counterhypothesis.reason: Current module explicitly does not contact providers or operate audio, so importing OpenAI-specific response/item/event vocabulary directly into the core contract would over-couple WP705 and violate its present abstraction boundary.

adjudication.why_distinct: Current WP705 proves transition-chain/session identity but not that provider conversation history equals actually heard assistant audio at interruption.

minimal_provider_neutral_evidence_candid.note: These are semantic roles, not mandated field names. OpenAI response_id/item_id/audio_end_ms are one adapter mapping. Other providers may use different mechanisms.

cases: model generates 3000 ms audio; client has played only 1200 ms when user begins speaking
BARGE_IN input identity is valid but no playback/truncation receipt exists
cancel succeeds but conversation truncation acknowledgement is missing
conversation truncation targets wrong assistant item
audio_end_ms exceeds locally observed played duration or targets a different response
all cancellation/playback/truncation identities align and only then barge-in re-entry is admitted
falsifier_for_trigger4_or_future_adapter.acceptance_invariant: No provider-bound BARGE_IN evidence may imply the user heard assistant content beyond independently observed local playback. Unheard generated audio/transcript must not survive into the provider conversation state used for re-entry when the provider offers an explicit truncation mechanism.
measurement: playback-cut acknowledgement where transport exposes one

model_selection_note.finding: Current OpenAI model catalog exposes newer realtime models including GPT-Realtime-2.1, while F2 WP705 remains correctly provider/model neutral. The contract should therefore bind provider/model identity at an adapter/runtime receipt boundary rather than hardcode one model into core evidence semantics.
